verses.text: Since we've been made right through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Through him, by faith, we've entered this grace where we stand. And we celebrate the hope of sharing God's glory.
And there's more: we can even find joy in our troubles, because we know trouble builds endurance,
endurance shapes proven character, and proven character grows hope.
This hope won't let us down, because God has poured his love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit he gave us.
While we were still helpless, at just the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
Hardly anyone would die for a righteous person—though someone might dare to die for a truly good person.
But God shows his love for us this way: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
So now that we've been made right by his blood, we will be saved from God's anger through him all the more.
If we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son while we were enemies, how much more, now that we're reconciled, will we be saved through his life!
And that's not all—we celebrate in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we've now received reconciliation.
Sin entered the world through one man, and death came through sin. In this way death spread to everyone, because everyone sinned.
Sin was already in the world before the law was given, but sin isn't counted as breaking a law when there is no law.
Even so, death ruled from Adam to Moses, including over people whose sin wasn't like Adam's disobedience. Adam was a pattern pointing to the one who was to come.
But the gift isn't like the trespass. If many died because of one man's trespass, God's grace and the gift that came through the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, overflowed to many even more.
The gift isn't like the result of one man's sin. Judgment from one trespass brought condemnation, but the gift after many trespasses brings people into right standing with God.
If death ruled through that one man's trespass, how much more will those who receive overflowing grace and the gift of righteousness rule in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!
So then, one trespass brought condemnation for everyone; in the same way, one righteous act brings justification and life for everyone.
Just as one man's disobedience made many sinners, one man's obedience will make many righteous.
The law came in so trespasses would increase. But where sin increased, grace overflowed even more,
so that just as sin ruled through death, grace might rule through righteousness and bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
